column1: # PROTEASE DEFINITIONS FILE
# Lines starting with '#' are comments and will be ignored by the parser.
# COLUMN DEFINITIONS (tab-separated):
# 1. Name                    - Unique identifier for the protease
# 2. Motif                   - Cleavage motif syntax defining where cleavage occurs (see below)
# 3. Specificity             - One of: full, semi, none, SingleN, SingleC
# 4. PSI-MS Accession        - Standard identifier (e.g., MS:1001313)
# 5. PSI-MS Name             - Standard name from PSI-MS ontology
# 6. Cleavage Modification   - Name of modification applied at cleavage site (optional)
# CUSTOM PROTEASES
# To add custom proteases (names that do not already exist in this file):
# 1. Create a TSV file with the same column format as this file
# 2. Call ProteaseDictionary.LoadAndMergeCustomProteases(path)
# Merge rules:
#   - If a protease name matches an existing entry (embedded or already-loaded custom),
#     the custom entry is SKIPPED and the existing definition is retained
#   - If a protease name is new, it will be ADDED to the dictionary
#   - The returned CustomDigestionAgentLoadResult lists which names were Added vs Skipped
# Example custom proteases file:
# Name
# MyCustomProtease
# MyTrypsinNoProline
# Both lines add new proteases. The second is a trypsin-like variant without proline restriction.
# (Note: The built-in trypsin|P has proline restriction via the [P] in its motif. A custom entry
# named "trypsin|P" would collide with the embedded definition and be skipped.)
# MOTIF SYNTAX GUIDE
# The motif syntax uses a simple pattern language:
# BASIC ELEMENTS:
#   |     = Cleavage point (where the peptide bond is cut)
#   X     = Any amino acid (wildcard)
#   A-Z   = Specific amino acid (single letter code)
#   B     = Aspartate (D) or Asparagine (N)
#   J     = Isoleucine (I) or Leucine (L)
#   Z     = Glutamate (E) or Glutamine (Q)
# POSITION RELATIVE TO CLEAVAGE:
#   K|    = Cleave AFTER lysine (C-terminal cleavage)
#   |K    = Cleave BEFORE lysine (N-terminal cleavage)
# PREVENTING CLEAVAGE (square brackets):
#   K[P]| = Cleave after K, UNLESS followed by P
#          (prevents cleavage when P is C-terminal to K)
# MULTIPLE MOTIFS (comma-separated):
#   "K[P]|,R[P]|" = Cleave after K or R, unless followed by P
# WILDCARD EXCLUSIONS (curly braces):
#   GPX{P}|GPX{P} = Match GPX|GPX pattern, but X cannot be P
# EXAMPLES
# Trypsin:     "K[P]|,R[P]|"  - Cleaves after K or R, not before P
# Asp-N:       |D             - Cleaves before D (N-terminal to D)
# Lys-C:       K[P]|          - Cleaves after K, not before P
# Non-specific: X|            - Cleaves after any residue
# Top-down:    (empty)        - No cleavage (intact protein)
# CLEAVAGE SPECIFICITY VALUES
# full    - Both termini must match cleavage rules
# semi    - Only one terminus must match cleavage rules
# none    - No enzymatic cleavage (top-down, peptidomics)
# SingleN - Single cleavage, N-terminal fragments only
# SingleC - Single cleavage, C-terminal fragments only
# SingleN/SingleC Example:
# Given a sequence "PEPTIDE", single cleavage produces ladder fragments:
#   SingleN (keeps N-terminus):     SingleC (keeps C-terminus):
#   P                               EPTIDE
#   PE                              PTIDE
#   PEP                             TIDE
#   PEPT                            IDE
#   PEPTI                           DE
#   PEPTID                          E
# PROTEASE DEFINITIONS

# O-GLYCOPROTEASES (mucinases)
# A GLYCOPROTEASE is any protease whose cleavage depends on the presence of
# glycosylation; MUCINASES are the subset selected for densely O-glycosylated
# mucin domains. Their rule has two halves -- a sequence motif AND a glycan
# required at a named Schechter-Berger subsite -- and until now this file could
# only express the first half.
# The optional "Cleavage Requirement" column carries the second half. It is
# written the way the literature writes a subsite: P<n> for the non-prime side,
# P<n>' for the prime side, then the modification class. So StcE is P2:O-glycan
# and the OgpA family is P1':O-glycan. The column is OPTIONAL and aliased -- a
# proteases.tsv written before it existed still loads, and its proteases simply
# declare no requirement.
# The requirement is honoured only when DigestionParams.
# RespectCleavagePromotingModifications is set, which defaults to FALSE. With it
# off the entries below match SEQUENCE ONLY, as StcE and StcE-trypsin always
# have, so they OVER-DIGEST relative to the real enzyme: their peptides are a
# superset of true StcE peptides. StcE-trypsin|P is StcE-trypsin with trypsin's
# proline rule and over-digests the same way.
# StcE, from enterohemorrhagic E. coli O157:H7 (MEROPS M66), cleaves in an
# S/T-X-S/T motif, severing the bond before the last residue, but ONLY when the
# FIRST S/T carries an alpha-O-GalNAc-initiated glycan -- that residue is P2.
# Activity is abolished by deglycosylation, and the requirement is specific to
# mucin-type glycans: the same peptide backbone carrying beta-O-GlcNAc instead of
# alpha-O-GalNAc is not cleaved, nor are O-mannosylated peptides. A glycan at P1'
# is permitted but NEVER required, which is why the motif below marks only P2.
#   Malaker et al., PNAS 2019, doi:10.1073/pnas.1813020116
# StcE is NOT an indiscriminate over-digester of glycoproteins: it does not
# cleave BSA, and it does not cleave several glycosylated non-mucins. Its
# selectivity for mucins is not a glycan-DENSITY rule, though -- a single
# glycosylated motif on a free 9-mer is cleaved -- but a consequence of the
# conformation dense O-glycosylation imposes, plus a separable C-terminal
# binding module. So a per-bond rule is the right model, and it will over-generate
# on folded non-mucin glycoproteins. That is a known and accepted limit.
# OpeRATOR (OgpA), IMPa and SmE are deliberately NOT listed yet. All three cleave
# N-terminal to a glycosylated Ser/Thr (P1':O-glycan), so with the flag off --
# the only setting MetaMorpheus can choose today -- each would be '|T,|S', a cut
# before EVERY Ser and Thr, which none of them makes. Their rows are written and
# tested in mzLib's test data (TestData/held-glycoproteases.tsv) and move here
# once MetaMorpheus can set the flag.
# A cell may hold several conditions separated by ";", all of which must hold;
# "!" marks one that FORBIDS rather than requires; and ">=" sets a minimum
# monosaccharide composition the glycan must contain.
# A composition floor can only be judged on a modification that carries a
# composition, and today nothing populates one. An unknown composition counts as
# meeting a REQUIRED floor and as not matching a FORBIDDEN one, so until
# compositions are populated a floor leaves its condition as it would be without
# one. What stays unencoded (identity, linkage, efficiency) costs search space and
# never an identification: a rule that admits glycoforms the enzyme would refuse
# proposes extra peptides, never fewer.
# In a composite entry the requirement attaches only to the motifs that have the
# named subsite, so StcE-trypsin carries the glycan rule on its four StcE motifs
# and none on K| or R|. A tryptic cut in a mixed digest is a tryptic cut.
